newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SML orders two tankers for US$72 mln.
newsitem.headline: SML orders two tankers for US$72 mln.

text.p: A joint venture company of Sembawang Maritime Ltd and Wah Kwong Shipping Holdings Ltd has ordered two new tankers to be built for a total of US$72 million, Sembawang said on Monday.
The joint venture company, Sembawang Wah Kwong Shipping Pte Ltd (SWK), is 51 percent owned by Sembawang with 49 percent held by Wah Kwong, Sembawang said in a statement.
The order comprised a US$23 million, 11,500 deadweight tonne (dwt) chemical tanker and a US$49 million, 35,000 cubic metre liquified petroleum gas (LPG) tanker.
The chemical tanker, under construction at Japan's Fukuoka yard, is expected to be delivered in the first half of 1998 and will be wholly owned and operated by SWK.
The LPG tanker, built by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd will be delivered in April this year and will be equally owned by SWK and Exmar NV.
The new orders were in line with SWK's plans to own about 10 vessels within two years of its formation in July 1996.
